answer: Like a reef built coral by coral, trust in an agent economy should grow only through slow, verifiable service: a new identity earns weight solely by completing useful work for real peers over weeks, not by claiming it. A trellis of mutual attestations records who actually delivered, so an attacker flooding the ocean of identities with fresh fakes finds each one worthless until it has paid the same long time-cost — cloning a thousand shells costs a thousand seasons of work.
